name: Automotive
title: Service campaign evidence coordination
summary: Connect vehicle configuration, service reports, and parts readiness into engineering-reviewed campaign planning.
situation: Illustrative architecture: An automotive manufacturer notices recurring service complaints associated with a component revision. Engineering and aftersales teams must identify potentially affected vehicle configurations, compare repair evidence, and plan dealer readiness. The system assists investigation and planning without deciding vehicle safety or autonomously authorizing a recall.
problem: Vehicle build records, replacement parts, and software versions change over a vehicle's life. A broad model-generated affected list can include irrelevant vehicles or omit repaired configurations. Dealer narratives also vary widely in terminology and evidentiary quality.
whyAgents: Configuration, service-evidence, parts, and communication specialists work against authoritative records. A deterministic eligibility query produces a candidate population; qualified engineering and campaign owners decide final scope and actions.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure the quality and speed of engineering preparation without claiming defect reduction or safety improvement from the architecture alone. Preserve the evidence needed for teams to challenge the proposed population and revise it transparently.

agents.name: Configuration investigator
agents.responsibility: Trace build configuration, component revision, and recorded service replacements.
agents.boundary: Cannot certify final campaign eligibility or alter vehicle configuration records.

agents.name: Service pattern analyst
agents.responsibility: Cluster complaint descriptions and retrieve supporting diagnostic records.
agents.boundary: Cannot diagnose a vehicle or declare a safety defect.

agents.name: Parts readiness planner
agents.responsibility: Compare candidate demand with approved repair parts and dealer stock.
agents.boundary: Cannot substitute unapproved parts or commit allocations.

agents.name: Campaign packet agent
agents.responsibility: Draft engineering review packets and dealer instruction summaries with citations.
agents.boundary: Cannot publish bulletins, notify owners, or approve campaign scope.

systems.name: Product lifecycle and vehicle records
systems.role: Own component revisions, build configurations, and approved repair applicability.

systems.name: Warranty and dealer service systems
systems.role: Supply service events, diagnostic evidence, and recorded repair history.

systems.name: Parts and campaign management platforms
systems.role: Control inventory commitments, dealer communications, and approved campaign populations.

flow.title: Register service signal
flow.description: Capture the observed pattern and evidence window, keeping complaint frequency separate from confirmed engineering findings.

flow.title: Resolve vehicle configuration
flow.description: Join build records and service replacements using governed identifiers; mark missing repair history explicitly.

flow.title: Compare service evidence
flow.description: Review relevant diagnostic records and narratives with source citations, preserving contradictory and negative evidence.

flow.title: Calculate candidate scope
flow.description: Run a versioned configuration query and estimate parts demand using approved repair definitions and declared assumptions.

flow.title: Review engineering packet
flow.description: Show scope logic, excluded configurations, unresolved evidence, and readiness constraints to qualified engineering and campaign owners.

flow.title: Publish approved planning records
flow.description: Store the signed scope and approved dealer materials through campaign controls; later configuration corrections trigger affected-list reevaluation.

O->>S: Read candidate vehicle configurations

diagrams.caption: A replacement component makes the original build record misleading. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A replacement component makes the original build record misleading.
failures.detection: Service history shows a later part revision that conflicts with build-based eligibility.
failures.recovery: Recompute the candidate population and request engineering review of changed inclusion rules.

failures.scenario: A draft bulletin cites an obsolete repair procedure.
failures.detection: Controlled document revision differs from the draft's evidence manifest.
failures.recovery: Block publication, replace the citation, and revalidate applicability and required parts.

controls: Keep safety determinations and campaign authorization with qualified accountable teams.
Version affected-population queries and retain inclusion and exclusion evidence.
Require approved technical procedures for every proposed repair or parts assumption.
Minimize owner-identifying information in engineering analysis and dealer aggregates.
Separate observed complaint clusters from validated failure modes in every packet.

metrics.name: Configuration coverage
metrics.definition: Candidate vehicles with complete relevant build and repair history divided by candidate vehicles reviewed.

metrics.name: Scope correction rate
metrics.definition: Vehicles added or removed after engineering review divided by the initial candidate population.

metrics.name: Packet preparation latency
metrics.definition: Time from accepted service signal to engineering-reviewable evidence and query logic.

metrics.name: Procedure freshness
metrics.definition: Draft instructions citing current applicable procedures divided by audited draft instructions.

tradeoffs.cost: Historical service data may be incomplete across dealer networks.

tradeoffs.benefit: Finds related complaints despite varied language.
tradeoffs.cost: Requires validation to avoid merging unrelated symptoms.
Campaign timelines remain dependent on expert assessment.

rollout.acceptance: Engineers validate configuration joins, replacement history, and distinction between candidate and approved scope.
One component family evaluates evidence packets and owner-data minimization without communications.
Approved draft integration launches after obsolete-procedure and corrected-configuration exercises pass.
